article.hook: You don’t hit first. You circle, wait, watch for the crack. Mars in Cancer shows how action can fold into care, not just force. It’s the kind of fight that feels like keeping someone safe, even if it’s yourself.
article.lived: For the next six weeks, drive sneaks in through the back door of feelings. We schedule extra calls to check on someone, send that text we almost deleted, or defend a boundary with quiet stubbornness. The push isn’t loud; it’s the slow burn of loyalty turning plans into promises that won’t break.
article.turn: That loyalty can twist into a wall you slam when hurt is ignored. Instead of naming pain, you ghost or snipe, acting from the hurt without admitting it. Protecting gets tangled with closing off, and the fight becomes a silent siege. Say what’s wrong or stay stuck behind your own barrier.
moves: Send one message you’ve held back because it feels risky.
Make a plan that defends your time like it’s a person.
Notice when you pull away instead of calling it out.
